original.target_description: Unassigned placeholder; not examined in this completion pass.

replication.target_description: Requested men-only ranking-task physical-attractiveness preference association with gender equality; source presents mixed-sex GDI interactions but does not print the men-only association or its analytic sample.

n.sample_role: Requested: men contributing to the men-specific association; available model N combines sexes.
n.exclusions: Whole-source exclusions: missing/out-of-range age, not exclusively heterosexual; rating incomplete traits; countries with fewer than 10 participants. No male analytic count printed for this target.
n.quote: This left us with a sample of 2986 participants from 36 countries for the ranking task, and 2524 participants from 30 countries for the rating data.

es.quote: Table 1. Results of tests for interactions between the effects of gender equality and participant sex in analyses controlling for Galton’s problem.

p.location: Results, paragraph introducing Table 1 and full-model-results link
p.quote: Full results for each of these models are given at https://osf.io/4sr5f/.

reported_success.location: Discussion, paragraph on gender equality and sex differences (no canonical page markers)
reported_success.quote: We saw no evidence that the sex difference in preference for physical attractiveness was greater in countries with greater gender equality.

notes: Only unfinished fields are assessed; original and unassigned fields are placeholders. No PDF supplied. The requested test concerns men’s own preference versus gender equality. Table 1 instead reports sex-by-gender-equality interactions, which do not identify the men-only slope; the printed main effect of participant sex is also a different test. Neither statistic is substituted. Candidate Table 1 interaction (not target): physical attractiveness | GDI | ranking | -0.25 | -0.60 | .55 Candidate common mixed-sex model N (not men-only analytic N): This left us with a sample of 2986 participants from 36 countries for the ranking task, and 2524 participants from 30 countries for the rating data. No N arithmetic or coefficient conversion performed. Source uses GII in place of GEM and Gender Development Index in place of the historical Gender-related Development Index. Full model results are linked externally but are not supplied and acquisition is prohibited. The discussion verdict concerns sex differences, not the men-only slope, so no reported_success is inferred.
